title: MGS3: A Multi-Granularity Self-Supervised Code Search Framework

problem.claim: Code search aims to retrieve code snippets relevant to natural-language queries to improve software reusability and developer productivity.

gap.claim: Existing self-supervised methods mainly align natural language with function-level code and overlook fine-grained block- and statement-level snippets, producing suboptimal performance across granularities.

contributions.claim: MGCodeSearchNet is a multi-granularity code search dataset containing more than 536K natural-language/code-snippet pairs.
MGS3 is a multi-granularity self-supervised contrastive-learning code search framework.

MGS3 uses hierarchical syntactic representations to aggregate fine-grained information into coarser-grained representations and constructs same-granularity positives and in-function negatives for fine-grained code.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly introduce MGS3 as a novel multi-granularity self-supervised contrastive-learning code search framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report outstanding performance across code search tasks at multiple granularities in experiments on code search benchmarks.
The authors report that MGS3 is model-agnostic and compatible with existing pretrained code representation models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Code search retrieves code relevant to natural-language queries for software reuse and developer productivity.
Prior self-supervised approaches emphasize function-level alignment and overlook finer-grained code snippets.
The authors create MGCodeSearchNet and propose MGS3 with hierarchical representations and granularity-aware contrastive samples.
Experiments are reported to perform strongly across granularities and to show model-agnostic compatibility.
